stories.title: Berlin's Russian House: A hub for propaganda and espionage?
stories.summary: The Russian House stands in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it's being used to spread propaganda for Putin's Russia. Now, French authorities have said it is being used by the Kremlin for espionage.

As a throwback to a bygone era of friendly German-Russian relations , it is the subject of fierce disagreements and has long been a bone of contention in Berlin . The massive seven-story building covering an area of almost 30,000 square meters opened in 1984. At that time, back in the days of the East German state , its role was to celebrate friendship with the Soviet Union through concerts, film screenings and book readings. It even had its own small bookstore. But now, more than 40 years later, French authorities have linked the building to possible activities by Russian intelligence services. stories.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Latvia
stories.summary: Jets have shot down a foreign drone over Latvia after it entered the Baltic state's airspace. Its origin remains unclear, but the incident adds to concern over repeated incursions along NATO's eastern flank.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IofK The Italian Eurofighter was scrambled from a base in neighboring Lithuania Image: GIUSEPPE LAMI/ANSA/picture alliance Advertisement NATO fighter jets have shot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the alliance and Latvian authorities said Friday. Two Italian Eurofighters were scrambled and one destroyed the unmanned aircraft, while two Turkish F-16s were also deployed under NATO command. What happened over Latvia? Latvia's military initially issued an air alert and urged people in affected areas to remain indoors and seek shelter. Authorities said the foreign drone entered Latvian airspace over the Balvi region as a result of Russian electronic warfare activity. It was not immediately clear where the drone originated, and NATO said an investigation was underway. Latvian authorities did not identify the drone as Ukrainian. However, the reference to Russian electronic warfare raised the possibility that a Ukrainian drone targeting Russia had been forced off course by interference. The Danube is the sole source of cooling water for the Cernavoda plant, which usually generates around one-fifth of Romania's electricity. The power station has only been shut down once before, in 2023, again as a result of drought and a hot summer . Meanwhile, Hungary was scrambling to dam the Danube, as it tries to keep its Paks nuclear power plant at least running at the minimal levels that it has maintained in recent days, which are far below capacity. stories.summary: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IiJH This year’s Eurovision Song Contest was won by Bulgaria’s entrant Dara, who won with her song "Bangaranga," meaning the 2027 contest will take place in the country for the first time Image: Georg Hochmuth/APA/AFP Advertisement Eurovision Song Contest organizers announced rule changes that would prevent countries involved in an armed conflict from hosting the event. Israel and Ukraine are among the countries the rule could affect, with both having enjoyed recent success in the competition. What did the Eurovision organizers say? Eurovision is typically staged by the broadcaster from the country that won the previous edition as part of a co-production involving members of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU). Around 1,200 residents and tourists were evacuated, while 10 people were in intensive care in hospital, the prime minister said.
